record.original_question: Let T be the 2-dimensional torus. A homeomorphism h: T -> T is called simple if it is supported on an embedded open disc, and the disc norm of h is the least number of simple homeomorphisms whose composition equals h. Do there exist homeomorphisms of T with arbitrarily large disc norm?

evidence.quote: A homeomorphism h: T → T is called simple if it is supported on an embedded open disc; that is, there is an embedded open disc Δ ⊂ T such that h is the identity outside of Δ.
The disc norm of a homeomorphism h: T → T is defined as the least number of simple homeomorphisms h1, . . . , hn such that h = h1 ◦ · · · ◦ hn.
Is there a homeomorphism of the 2-dimensional torus with arbitrarily large disc norm?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $T = \mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2$ denote the 2-dimensional torus. A homeomorphism $h\colon T \to T$ is called \emph{simple} if there exists an embedded open disc $\Delta \subset T$ (i.e., the image of an embedding of the open unit disc into $T$) such that $h$ is the identity on $T \setminus \Delta$; equivalently, $h$ is supported on $\Delta$. For a homeomorphism $h\colon T \to T$ that can be written as a finite composition of simple homeomorphisms, define the \emph{disc norm} of $h$ to be
$$\|h\| = \min\{\, n \geq 0 : h = h_1 \circ h_2 \circ \cdots \circ h_n \text{ with each } h_i \text{ simple}\,\}.$$
Question: Does there exist a sequence of homeomorphisms $\{h_k\}_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ of $T$ such that $\|h_k\| \to \infty$ as $k \to \infty$? Equivalently, is the disc norm unbounded on the group of those homeomorphisms of $T$ for which it is finite?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears in a recent (October 2025) collection of open problems in geometry. A targeted web search did not turn up any solution or partial result establishing unboundedness of the disc norm on the 2-torus, so the question appears to remain open.
